meta.title: Hofwerk — Project Knowledge Graph
meta.description: Physical project, timeline, people, places. Specific to the Anhalt farmstead.

nodes.label: The Hofwerk Project
nodes.description: Three-sided farmstead (Dreiseitenhof) in Anhalt, East Germany. Built 1884 (Wilhelmine period), GDR additions. Acquired November 30, 2020. 1h SW of Berlin by train + bike.

nodes.label: Joachim Broecher
nodes.description: Professor, University of Flensburg. Dept. of Social and Emotional Learning. Former teacher and school principal (20 years). Scientific documentation and concept development.

nodes.label: Philipp Broecher
nodes.description: Project lead. Manual labor, photo editing. Based in Lucerne, Switzerland.

nodes.label: Broecher Family
nodes.description: Family-funded project. Karin-Anna Jung-Broecher (interior/exterior design, landscaping), Jan Broecher (Berlin).

nodes.label: Tomasz (Character Prototype)
nodes.description: Young man from the Beskids/Carpathians. Lemko ethnic minority. Homeschooled by Andrzej. Practical, nature-oriented. Now working with Paweł in South Tyrol on historic mountain farms.

nodes.label: Ludwik (Character Prototype)
nodes.description: Young pedagogue from Sopot, Poland. Lithuanian noble ancestry. Gifted pianist (Chopin, Liszt, Schubert). Left Polish school system. Now gives piano lessons in Berlin.

nodes.label: Ragnar (Character Prototype)
nodes.description: Composite character. 25 years old, from Hoyerswerda area, Saxony. Left school early, no certificate. Works collecting scrap metal. Physically strong, practically skilled. Met in a DIY store.

quotes.text: Ragnar is for me what Emile was for Jean-Jacques Rousseau. At the same time, Ragnar is quite real, because he is made up of facets of several young men with whom I have actually worked.

nodes.label: Paweł
nodes.description: Tomasz's uncle. Highly skilled carpenter and roofer. Itinerant craftsman (Switzerland, Austria, South Tyrol). Built roofs, enhanced cultural life through Polish literature discussions.

nodes.label: Andrzej Jaczewski
nodes.description: Centenarian. Pediatrician, teacher, professor (Warsaw, Krakow). Pioneer of German-Polish educational exchange. Homeschooled Tomasz. Died October 2021. The grand presence behind the project.

nodes.label: Cooperation Partners
nodes.description: Local architect Uwe Kelling (Leitzkau), energy consultant André König (Dessau), farmer Jörn Friedrich (Dobritz), and ~20 local companies and craftsmen.

nodes.label: Farmhouse
nodes.description: Living quarters. Cellar (sand under parts). 1884 coffered doors. Three tiled stoves (yellow, etc.). Five chimneys. GDR-era bathroom addition. Small kitchen with hotplates.

nodes.label: Barn
nodes.description: Spacious interior. Former chicken coop. Hayloft. Historical Wilhelmine windows installed. Hosts seminars, discussions, cultural events. Climbing and gymnastics space.

nodes.label: Workshop
nodes.description: Cleaned of decades of debris. Anvil and workbench retained. New sandwich panel roof (built by Paweł). Smart technologies + old manual techniques.

nodes.label: Stable Building
nodes.description: Major reconstruction and extension. Plans: commercial space (street side), accessible apartment, kitchen/living room, four guest rooms with bathrooms upstairs. Building permit granted.

nodes.label: Secondary Structures
nodes.description: GDR-era garage, former pigpen (torn down), small stalls and sheds (some demolished). Asbestos roof removed by specialists.

nodes.label: Farmyard (Innenhof)
nodes.description: Central courtyard. Fieldstone paving under 100+ years of soil. Sewage pipes excavated and replaced. Cherry tree. Lavender planter with butterflies.

nodes.label: South Facing Field
nodes.description: Wooden deck built by Philipp and Tomasz. Red fir oil weatherproofing. For reading, music, language learning, cloud-watching. Winter brazier.

nodes.label: Gardens
nodes.description: Behind the barn. Wolf habitat. Horticultural experiments. Straw from renovation used as path covering.

nodes.label: Pastures
nodes.description: Currently fallow — supporting biodiversity. Insects, birds, small creatures. Future potential for livestock.

nodes.label: Fruit Trees
nodes.description: Cherry, plum, apple, pear, peach trees. Surplus shared with neighbors. Ecological jam, fruit cake, juice production started.

nodes.label: Walnut Tree
nodes.description: Planted by Philipp. Gnawed by hare/deer. Protected with reinforcing fabric and stakes. Nursed back to health. A meditative, long-term act of care.

nodes.label: Benjes Hedge
nodes.description: Dead hedge made from branches and cuttings. Habitat for wildlife. Ongoing maintenance.

nodes.label: Water Supply
nodes.description: Broken pipes in cellar at acquisition. Copper lines replaced. No lead pipes (checked). Rainwater collection planned. Well with electric pump.

nodes.label: Heating — Tiled Stoves & Firewood
nodes.description: Three tiled stoves (6-8 hours to warm). Firewood from property. First winter: minus 5°C indoors, sleeping in wool hats. Heat generation and timber industry.

nodes.label: Electrical
nodes.description: Partial grid working at acquisition. Elektro Runge (Schweinitz) for installation work.

nodes.label: Sewage
nodes.description: Old pipes excavated and replaced (May 2023). Stable building connected to sewer. Cesspool from pre-sewer era still present.

nodes.label: Future Energy
nodes.description: Heat pump, solar cells, small wind turbine under consideration. Energy consulting by André König.

nodes.label: Renovation & Construction
nodes.description: Ongoing since Nov 2020. Roofing, guttering, stable reconstruction, debris removal, asbestos disposal, brick work, plastering. Heritage preservation alongside modernization.

nodes.label: Agriculture & Food
nodes.description: Fruit harvesting, jam/juice production, garden experiments, tree care, scything. Surplus shared with neighbors.

nodes.label: Cultural Life
nodes.description: Music (heroic film scores, Chopin, classical), furniture making/restoring, designs and objects, conviviality by the tiled stove with Belgian winter beer.

nodes.label: Polish-German Connection
nodes.description: Polish literature central (Tokarczuk, Huelle, Gombrowicz, Reymont, Brandys, Kuczok, Schulz, Sienkiewicz). Language learning. Emotional and social geographies. Cold War educational exchange legacy.

quotes.text: Polish literature moved more and more into focus on our farm, so that our first cultural life unfolded around it.

nodes.label: Seminars & Think Tank
nodes.description: Informal seminars in the barn. Focus on biographies, generations, communities of the future. University classes streamed during Covid. Polish language courses.

nodes.label: Timeline
nodes.description: Key milestones in the project's development.

nodes.label: 2020 — Acquisition
nodes.description: Late autumn: farmstead purchased. Keys handed over November 30, 2020. First winter: camping in rooms with tiled stoves, sleeping bags, foam mats.

nodes.label: 2021 — First Steps
nodes.description: Basic cleanup, debris removal, improvised living. First texts published. Tomasz arrives from Poland. Water pipes fixed. Ant nest dealt with.

nodes.label: 2022 — Building Momentum
nodes.description: Paweł arrives — new roofs for workshop and bathroom. Wooden deck built. Furniture restored. First seminars. Tomasz Vol. 1 documents progress to May 2022.

nodes.label: 2023 — Going Public
nodes.description: Frontiers in Sociology article published (May). Ludwik Vol. 2 published. Stable building gutted and reconstruction begins. Sewage pipes replaced. Building permit granted. Ragnar enters the scene.

nodes.label: 2024 — Expansion
nodes.description: Ragnar Vol. 3 published (August, e-paper). Stable reconstruction continues. Monthly journal May 2023 – August 2024 documented.

nodes.label: Frontiers in Sociology Article
nodes.description: Broecher & Painter (2023). Peer-reviewed. Open access.

nodes.label: Tomasz — Vol. 1
nodes.description: 436 illustrations. Print and e-book. Available in EN, DE, IT, PL.

nodes.label: Ludwik — Vol. 2
nodes.description: ~280 illustrations. Print and e-book. Available in EN, DE, PL.

nodes.label: Ragnar — Vol. 3
nodes.description: ~400 photos. Digital only (e-paper on ResearchGate). Published August 30, 2024.

nodes.label: De Gruyter Volume
nodes.description: Transformative Community-Projekte. 192 pages, 100 color illustrations. Academic publisher. December 2025.

nodes.label: YouTube Channel
nodes.description: Film recordings documenting changes to site and buildings over time.

nodes.label: Similar Projects (Research)
nodes.description: Projects in the region or with similar philosophy. Not yet cooperating — for research and inspiration only.
